subject: Persistent response tails impacting checkout — capacity & mitigation plan
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@azura-retail.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Azura Infra <infra@azura-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Checkout p99 spikes — started 10/18 evening

Hi Kimberly,

We're seeing sustained p99 spikes on Redwood calls used in our checkout flow since ~10/18 21:00 PDT. Baseline p99 has historically been ~450ms; over the last 18 hours it's been bouncing between 1.5s and 6s and we've had several customer checkouts time out (some 504s). Throughput to the Redwood route has dropped (we're seeing retries and fallbacks on our side).

Key notes:
- Affected route: /v1/generate (model: rwd-13b-prod)
- Error spikes correlate with increased request queue length reported in our client logs
- No code change on our side between 10/17–10/18 other than a config flip that increased per-worker concurrency for async workers (we're investigating)

This is directly impacting live checkout traffic for our holiday pilots. Can you confirm whether this looks like a capacity/queueing/backpressure issue on Redwood's side (concurrency caps, KV cache pressure, or request admission)? We need an urgent mitigation plan — even a temporary knob to reduce tail latency (per-tenant cap or throttling) would help.

Appreciate urgency — happy to hop on a call.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Engineering
Azura Retail
liam.oconnor@azura-retail.com
+1 415-555-0182

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Checkout p99 spikes — urgent triage

Team — forwarding Azura's note. High business impact (checkout). They're seeing long-tail response spikes and queue buildup.

Immediate asks:
- Dylan: can you lead root cause on queue/backpressure and KV cache behaviour for Azura's tenant (rwd-13b-prod)? Start with request queue depth, per-tenant concurrency, prefix/KV cache hit/miss rates and any recent routing changes.
- Vivek: validate whether any autoscaling or slot allocation events happened in the last 24 hrs for the region serving Azura. Check dedicated slot availability and slow drain events.
- Monica: own external comms — I'll approve a short status note once we have an action plan.

Proposed immediate mitigations to consider (we can pick what to implement quickly):
1) Apply a temporary per-tenant concurrency cap (e.g., 16) to reduce request pileup
2) Enable admission control fill rate for that route for 1–2 hours
3) Immediate hot-key sharding and flush for the kvcache if we see thrashing
4) If needed, provision a short burst of dedicated slots for Azura (ask sales/exec)

Attaching the traces they sent (azura_p99_traces_20261019.png) for context. Let's meet in 30 minutes (09:55 PT) to align.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Checkout p99 spikes — urgent triage

Short summary of what I see from the telemetry:
- p95 for the route is still ~220ms; p99 is ~3.9s across the last 6 hours, with spikes up to 6s matching Azura's logs.
- Request queue depth for tenant AZR (shard eu-west-1/zone-3) climbed steadily starting 2026-10-18T21:05:00Z. Current queue length peaked at ~1.8k items and is now around ~900 after intermittent drops.
- KV cache: high eviction and miss rate over the same window — looks like repeated large prompt prefixes are causing KV cache thrashing and lock contention on the serving nodes. kvcache_dump_20261019.txt attached.
- Notable: Azura's client-side telemetry (provided) shows a recent client change that increased concurrent outstanding requests per worker from 8 -> 64; that maps to a surge of parallel requests into the serving pool which our admission control hadn't curtailed for this tenant specifically.

Short-term mitigations I recommend and can execute in the next hour:
A) Apply a per-tenant concurrency cap = 16 (will drop parallelism and should reduce queueing within a minute). Owner: Dylan (I can flip this). ETA: 10–15m to implement and monitor.
B) Enable admission-control admission window for AZR route to smooth bursts (rate-limit threshold to be tuned). Owner: Dylan/Vivek. ETA: 20–45m.
C) Hot-shard the kvcache for AZR keys (reduce lock collisions). This requires a short cache shard flip that will cause a transient cold-cache hit rate increase but eliminate thrashing. Owner: Infra (Vivek) with Dylan. ETA: 45–90m depending on coordination.
D) If we see no improvement, spin a short-term extra slot allocation (2–4 slots) on the dedicated pool serving Azura. That needs Exec approval for cost. Owner: Kimberly/Marissa.

I'll apply (A) now and monitor p99. I'll push findings in the thread in 15 minutes.

--
Dylan
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@azura-retail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout p99 spikes — urgent triage

Hi Liam — thanks for flagging this and for the traces.

Short plan we are implementing immediately:
- We've applied a temporary per-tenant concurrency cap of 16 for Azura. This reduces parallel outstanding requests and should shrink the queue within minutes.
- Dylan + Vivek are enabling admission-control smoothing on the affected route and will hot-shard the kvcache to remove lock contention.
- We will monitor p99 and checkout error rates continuously and revert or adjust knobs as needed.

Ask from Azura: if you can temporarily revert the client-side concurrency flip (64 -> 8) or add exponential backoff on retries while we stabilize, that will speed recovery. If not possible immediately, we'll proceed with the server-side caps.

I'll post a 30-minute update and set up a short joint call if you prefer.

Thanks — Kim

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@azura-retail.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Azura Infra <infra@azura-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout p99 spikes — urgent triage

Kim — thanks. We'll roll the client concurrency back to 8 on our side (deploy in the next 20m) and will add backoff on retry loops. Please proceed with the caps and sharding — we authorize temporary measures including caps or slot bumps. We appreciate the quick response; Black Friday load test next week makes this high priority.

— Liam

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Executive note — Azura checkout p99 escalation (post-stabilization status)

Rishi/Marissa — quick exec summary and ask:

Impact: Azura experienced p99 spikes (up to 6s) that caused checkout timeouts and reduced throughput during 2026-10-18 21:00 - 2026-10-19 11:00 PT. They run critical holiday pilots and a Black Friday load test next week.

What we did:
- Applied per-tenant concurrency cap (16) and admission smoothing; hot-sharded kvcache.
- Azura rolled client concurrency back from 64->8 as requested.
- Observed p99 drop from ~3.9s -> ~420ms within ~45 minutes of interventions.

Remaining asks / decisions:
1) Azura has asked for a temporary dedicated-slot bump (2 slots) for the week of the Black Friday test. Estimated incremental cost for 1 week: $13k. Approval needed for sales to provision.
2) We should own a short postmortem with corrective actions in our infra to avoid tenant-caused endemic kvcache thrashing: admission-control defaults, better per-tenant backpressure signals, and a guardrail for client-configured concurrency.

Recommendation: approve temporary slot bump (Marissa to review pricing) and commit SRE/Platform to a short project to harden per-tenant admission controls (Dylan/Vivek to draft scope).

Status: issue stabilized; customer is back to normal traffic and will run a load test next week. I'll coordinate the postmortem once SRE has the first-draft RCA.

-Kim
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
